title: Copperlane onramp: hosted vs dedicated vs VPC evaluation
summary: Intro discovery focused on time-to-first-token (TTFT) via Redwood PLG API, evaluation of hosted vs Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private VPC/on-prem options. Customer has latency-sensitive inference paths for product search and support summarization, wants security/compliance context and a rough cost/throughput comparison. Agreed next step: Redwood to share pilot pricing, SSO/SAML doc, and a short benchmark plan for a 7-day hosted pilot with optional Dedicated trial.
topics: TTFT and free credits for PLG onboarding
Hosted API vs Dedicated (reserved capacity) vs Private VPC
Security: KMS, SSO, audit logs, retention
questions: How quickly can Copperlane get to a token in dev?
What controls exist for customer data in hosted mode?
When does Dedicated make sense vs Private?
Are there rate limits and quota bump processes?
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-01-12 16:00 PST
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Tori Kim (Redwood CSM); Alyssa Chen (CTO, Copperlane), Marcus Reed (Platform Eng), Nora Vidal (Head of ML), Ben Ortiz (Legal)

Summary / Notes: quick discovery to map TTFT path and surface security questions; customer leaning PLG to validate product but expects to move to Dedicated or VPC for regulated flows.

00:00:00 Jordan Miles: Hey everyone thanks for joining. we're Jordan on the account, Samir our solutions engineer, and Tori from success. how's everyone doing?
00:00:08 Alyssa Chen: good thanks. we've got about 45 minutes. want to boil this down — we need to know: how fast can our engineers call your API and get responses, and what tradeoffs when we hit production volumes.
00:00:20 Jordan Miles: perfect. that's exactly what we want to cover. quick round: how are you calling LLMs today? are you already on an API?
00:00:28 Marcus Reed: right now we run a mix. some models are hosted — we use a public API for prototyping, and we also run a couple of quantized models on prem for latency-critical inference. it's a pain to manage.
00:00:40 Nora Vidal: and our search reranking and tagline generator are the two highest-volume low-latency paths. for search we want 200ms p95 ideally, for generation we can tolerate up to 800ms.
00:00:52 Samir Patel: ok noted. two velocity questions then — TTFT for dev and ramp to prod. for TTFT we usually offer free onboarding credits (we call them token credits) and a self-serve path that typically gets engineering to first token inside a day if they follow our quickstart.
00:01:07 Alyssa Chen: day is great. what does that quickstart look like?
00:01:10 Samir Patel: short answer: signup, get API key, run one curl or SDK sample to hit the hosted endpoint, and you stream or poll results. we provide sample prompt templates and a tiny infra recipe for retry/backoff. includes client libs in Python/Node. most teams hit first token in a few hours; with CI and a simple integration it's a day.
00:01:26 Marcus Reed: and the free credits — size? expiration?
00:01:29 Jordan Miles: we can offer an initial credits pack to run your smoke tests and a small pilot. typical is $X of credits for 30 days — I'll share exact numbers — and we can extend for a short hosted trial if you need more runway.
00:01:41 Nora Vidal: ok. security — our legal and infra teams care about data residency, audit logs, and KMS. when you say hosted, what controls do we actually get?
00:01:51 Tori Kim: good question. hosted gives you the fastest TTFT and is the PLG path. controls include per-token logging toggles, token-level cost and latency breakdowns in the Console, and options to disable customer-visible logs. for encryption we integrate with managed KMS for key rotation; we also have enterprise packages for bring-your-own-key depending on region.
00:02:13 Ben Ortiz: do you have SOC 2 or ISO attestation?
00:02:16 Tori Kim: yes, SOC 2 Type II and we can share our audit pack. for Private deployments we offer VPC and on-prem which gives you full network isolation and your own control plane.
00:02:25 Marcus Reed: that's the pivot question — when should we move to Dedicated or VPC? we want predictable throughput for search reranking.
00:02:33 Samir Patel: Dedicated is reserved capacity — think of it as dedicated GPU pools for your tenant with autoscaling policy you configure. it's ideal if you need predictable p95s and unit economics. Private (VPC/on-prem) is when you need network isolation, region-specific residency, or can't use a shared control plane for compliance reasons.
00:02:50 Alyssa Chen: performance — curious how caching and batching work. our current on-prem setup uses KV caching aggressively.
00:02:57 Samir Patel: we have automatic prefix and KV cache support; for search reranking you can cache embeddings and KV state to avoid recompute. continuous batching is tunable — you can bias for latency or throughput. our runtime also chooses kernels based on model and seq length so we get better perf than naive runtimes.
00:03:16 Marcus Reed: earlier you said 200ms p95 for search is achievable — is that on hosted or Dedicated?
00:03:22 Samir Patel: depends on model size and sequence lengths. for a smaller transformer optimized for low latency on GPU, 200ms p95 is achievable on Dedicated with a configured instance type and low batching. Hosted can get there too for modest volume, but Dedicated gives you the guarantee and SLA.
00:03:35 Alyssa Chen: any noisy neighbors on hosted?
00:03:37 Jordan Miles: we use smart routing and policy-based placement; for higher SLAs you move to Dedicated. Hosted is multi-tenant but we provide SLO-backed latency tiers for pros.
00:03:46 Nora Vidal: about cost — rough delta between hosted and Dedicated?
00:03:50 Jordan Miles: roughly, hosted is pay-as-you-go per token, whereas Dedicated is a reservation with lower unit cost at commit. I'll put precise pricing options in the follow-up but expect a step down in unit cost at the price of a commit. we can run a cost simulation for your QPS profile.
00:04:06 Marcus Reed: legal asks about data deletion and retention — how do you handle logs and training data usage?
00:04:11 Tori Kim: by default we don't use customer prompts to continue training models; we can offer No-Taint guarantees in enterprise plans and a retention policy for logs with configurable retention windows and exportable audit logs.
00:04:23 Ben Ortiz: good. can we get a packet with SAML, KMS, and retention policies?
00:04:27 Tori Kim: yes will include that.
00:04:30 Jordan Miles: next, pilot proposal. we recommend a 7-14 day hosted pilot using your smoke tests to validate latency and correctness, followed by a short Dedicated trial if you want throughput guarantees. does that plan sound reasonable?
00:04:42 Alyssa Chen: yes. timeline wise we want something next sprint — two weeks — to run smoke tests.
00:04:47 Jordan Miles: great. will put a proposed schedule: day 0-1 signup + key + run smoke tests; day 2-4 iterate on prompts and routing; day 5-7 run load tests and collect metrics.
00:04:58 Nora Vidal: if we move to Dedicated, what's the minimum commit or lead time?
00:05:02 Samir Patel: depends on region and capacity. typical lead time is a couple weeks for Dedicated provisioning; we can do short bursts sooner. we'll be explicit in the SOW.
00:05:12 Marcus Reed: any SDK gotchas for our stack? we use Go and Python, but mostly Go on the backend.
00:05:18 Samir Patel: we have Python/Node official SDKs. Go users typically use the HTTP API or a thin wrapper; Samir: we can share a Go example and a small library we've seen customers use.
00:05:30 Alyssa Chen: are there rate limits that will affect our CI tests?
00:05:33 Jordan Miles: hosted has default rate limits but they are adjustable for pilots; Dedicated removes shared rate-limiting constraints per tenant. we'll include quota bump process in the follow-up.
00:05:44 Ben Ortiz: ok legal review after we see SOC and retention.
00:05:47 Jordan Miles: understood. quick recap and actions?
00:05:50 Jordan Miles: we'll share: 1) pilot pricing and initial credits offer, 2) SOC 2 and security packet including SAML/KMS docs, 3) a one-page benchmark plan for the 7-day hosted pilot, 4) Go examples and SDK snippets, 5) Dedicated commit options and timelines.
00:06:08 Alyssa Chen: that covers it. Marcus and Nora will run the smoke tests. Ben will review security docs.
00:06:14 Jordan Miles: awesome. we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the kick-off and a readout at the end of the week. thanks everyone.

End of meeting transcript. There are some intermittent transcription errors in the recording (names sometimes merged) — please treat verbatim moments as approximate.
